chapter_title: Concerning the Fourteen Vehicles that Jesus has boarded.
chapter_note: The chapter’s core is a systematic cosmological listing of ten “vehicles/carriages” (¶2–8) in which Jesus the Son of Greatness journeys through the cosmic orders. A clear editorial seam then extends the pattern to the institutional church (¶9). The closing paragraph (¶10) begins as a structural arithmetic summary (likely closing the older list) but then shifts into later soteriological/praise material (beatitude-style blessing and polemical antithesis). Strong editorial fatigue signal aligns with the late ecclesial extension and closing exhortative tone.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic discourse-frame (“Once again… speaks…”) introducing a public teaching scene; hagiographic/editorial container rather than systematic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: When Jesus the Son of Greatness came to these worlds, at the time that he unveiled the greatness, he boarded ten vehicles. He journeyed in the universe by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mission statement introducing a numbered/ordered list of vehicles; no NT citation formula. “Jesus the Son of Greatness” functions as a Manichaean cosmic being-title within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The first vehicle is the light ship, since he received instructions from the Ambassador there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/list structure (“first…”) mapping Jesus’ descent-movement to a cosmic station (“light ship”) and a named cosmic figure (“Ambassador”).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.37⟩ The second carriage is the ship of the First Man, since his dwelling is established there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues systematic enumeration; internal cosmological geography and a principal Iranian-Manichaean entity (“First Man”).

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man, since he shone forth there. He came below, he appeared in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the cosmological itinerary: station-name + functional explanation. The voice remains expository, not hortatory or institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the summons that he clothed upon his body. The fifth is the obedience that he swathed upon the summons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Abstract cosmic process-elements (“summons/obedience”) treated as assumable ‘garments’ in a fixed sequence—typical core mechanism language.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth is the living air, and since he assumed it too, he received anointment there. The seventh is the living wind that blows. The eighth is the light that illuminates. The ninth is the living water. The tenth is the living fire that is above them all.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold elemental run (air/wind/light/water/fire) embedded in the numbered vehicle scheme; cosmos→cosmos mapping with no institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: He was journeying in these ten carriages among all the orders and all the [...], those above and those below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding cosmic scope statement for the tenfold sequence (“orders… above… below”); still internal to the system and closes the list-unit.

Editorial seam/extension: after the tenfold cosmic list is complete, the pattern is continued into institutional identifications (“holy church… brothers… sisters… catechumens”). By rule, the entire paragraph is a late ecclesial graft, not MIXED.

paragraphs.core_text: These ten carriages that he boarded in the zone, and the other four that are in the flesh, they complete and make fourteen carriages.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ensuing soteriological/praise and beatitude material (“He has done in them… Blessed is he…”) as a later concluding exhortative/doxological overlay on the list, shifting from structural enumeration to salvation-polemics and blessing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a structural arithmetic closure of the list (ten + four = fourteen), matching the core’s enumerative logic; then pivots into evaluative/praise language (“Blessed is he…”, antithesis of ‘his’ vs ‘strangers’) characteristic of later editorial conclusion rather than the impersonal mapping style.
